meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 무대를 비워둘 순 없죠, 무대는 제가 지킬 테니까 다녀오세요 국장님!

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean suffix/syllable found in prestigious professions like 의사 ('doctor') and 판사 ('judge')

examples.trans: Both 'doctor' and 'lawyer' end in the syllable 'sa'.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Describes physical or mental tiredness.

examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (take a break, rest).

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.text: 그냥 내버려 둬, 쟤 완전 취했어.

examples.text: 승찬이 그 선배한테 완전 갈굼당하고 있는 거 아니야?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (interj).

examples.trans: Yeah, she was pretty—and I asked her out for a second date too.
Here the word for 'yeah' is key.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?

meanings.note: in expressions like 뭔 소리야? ('what are you talking about?')

examples.trans: You always say you are a tough woman, senior, yet my conclusion after watching beside you for two months is that you are not all that tough.

examples.text: 항상 준비하면 좋은 결과가 나올 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (always), good results will follow.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.

Did you hear about this female?

meanings.note: Common verb for expressing thoughts in words.

examples.trans: Please speak slowly.
Speak loudly.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.en: to pass (of time) or go past (a place)
meanings.note: Its adnominal form 지난 ('past / last') is commonly used before time nouns, e.g., 지난 시즌.

examples.trans: Time passes really fast.
I watched a movie last weekend.

meanings.note: Attributive form of 둘 used directly before counter nouns (두 개, 두 사람).

examples.text: 선배는 항상 나는 센 여자다라고 말하시지만, 제가 지난 두 달간 지켜보며 내린 결론은 선배는 그리 센 분이 아닙니다.

meanings.note: Used as progressive -고 (지켜보고).

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

meanings.note: commonly used with -에 (옆에)

meanings.note: verb to understand

meanings.note: When used with 알다/모르다, it means knowing or not knowing a fact or how to do something.

meanings.note: Interrogative determiner placed directly before a noun.

examples.trans: What kind of movies do you like?
Some person called.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.note: Used colloquially as an adverb meaning 'truly'.

examples.text: 나 진짜 들킨 연예인 된 기분이야.

meanings.note: Introduces a contrast, unexpected turn, or new topic. In everyday speech it is very often contracted to 근데. RR: geureonde; spoken geunde.

examples.trans: Someone once told me my true feelings always show, yet the sincerity everyone else spots never seems to get noticed by you.

examples.text: 이번에는 꼭 제대로 해 보고 싶어요, 들켜지다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: This time I really want to do it right (get noticed / discovered).

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.
